newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan newspaper suspended in party dispute.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan newspaper suspended in party dispute.

text.p: A Moroccan court has suspended Anoual newspaper, mouthpiece of the opposition Organisation of Democratic and Popular Action (OADP), in a political dispute between party leaders, a court official said on Monday.
The suspension coincided with a referendum on constitutional reforms on Friday. The vote triggered fighting within the OADP leaders with some backing the reforms and others opposing.
Moroccans overwhelmingly backed the reforms with 99.56 percent "yes" ballots.
"The decision to suspend Anoual newspaper was taken by the court after its (the paper's) director Abdellatif Awad asked the authorities to legally proceed with the suspension," the official said.
Awad is one of the party leaders who backed the reforms.
The OADP, breaking ranks with three other main opposition parties, asked its supporters to vote "no" in the referendum.
Asked about Anoual's suspension, Interior Minister Driss Basri said: "The government has nothing to do with the internal disputes of Moroccan parties."
